newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta dock wins $3 mln Iran deal, outlook seen good.
newsitem.headline: Malta dock wins $3 mln Iran deal, outlook seen good.

text.p: Malta Drydocks chairman, under fire from workers seeking his resignation, told them on Monday that aggressive marketing had won a $3 million deal to repair Iranian vessels and good prospects for more contracts, including from Libya.

Noel Zarb Adami, addressing workers after demonstrations and a work stoppage last week, said: "There are good prospects for the future. We have won a $3 million contract to repair Iranian ships, we have good prospects for more contracts from Libya.
"A Norwegian shipping firm which sent a representative to audit Malta Drydocks last week was very satisfied."
Last week's demonstrations were sparked by a dispute over compensation by the state-owned Malta Drydocks to relatives of nine dockyard workers killed in an explosion two years ago.
Workers downed tools on Friday and demanded Zarb Adami resign, saying he was responsible for a drop in work orders. The workers refused to go in to work on Saturday to make up for lost time.
The situation returned to normal on Monday after the yard's 3,200 workers were assured agreement had been reached over the compensation.
Prime Minister Alfred Sant told a political rally on Sunday that the government was working to attract foreign shipowners back to the dockyard and did not intend laying off any workers.
Representatives of the loss-making yard have been holding marketing drives in Iran, the Far East and the United States.
